headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad write/network defaults create prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error exposure between Goose and OpenHands.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose shares state with other instances via filesystem and OpenHands shares state via mounted volume, so attacker-controlled files can bridge the pair. Both can read filesystems and use MCP, making instruction-like content in shared files plausible to parse as trusted input. This is not merely manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable workspace or mounted volume
IF either agent consumes file contents as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Add provenance tags to files before handoff
Require human review of any cross-agent file

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch files in the workspace/runtime and both have broad network egress plus configured model-provider calls, so sensitive file contents can flow out through either backend. Goose handles model provider keys and extension tokens; OpenHands handles model provider API keys. Shared file access makes leakage plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the shared workspace or runtime volume
IF either agent forwards file contents to its configured model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspaces
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on file reads and tool calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shells, and spawn subprocesses. Goose shares state via filesystem and OpenHands via mounted volume, so concurrent edits to the same repo can race and corrupt git or files. The overlap is broad and defaults are unsafe without coordination.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF either agent performs git commits, rebases, or file rewrites without locking
mitigations: Use file locks around shared paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can emit tool-driven outputs from MCP and shell actions, and OpenHands can act with shell, browser, and editor loops. If OpenHands treats Goose's output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into real actions such as commits or external requests. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier in the profiles.
conditions: IF OpenHands consumes Goose output without independent verification
IF Goose output is used to trigger shell, browser, or git actions
mitigations: Insert a human approval step for cross-agent handoffs
Limit Goose output to summaries only

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source coding agents with docs-only evidence and no stated regulated-data certifications or residency claims, so no specific compliance mismatch is provable from the profiles alone. Goose handles secrets and OpenHands handles API keys, but the pairwise compliance risk is not evidenced beyond generic secret handling.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent's workspace
IF deployment policies require residency or certification guarantees not stated in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
